messages:
taylor: Heads-up — FluxPay Dedicated pool started returning 429s and high token latency around 09:20 UTC. Customer reports spike in TPS. Seen admission_control logs showing burst_credits=0 and lots of `admission:reject` entries.

samir: Can you paste the admission log lines and the pool config? also which model variant they hit?

support_junior: Pasting a few relevant snippets from the live logs:```
2026-03-17T09:19:54Z admission:accept id=abc123 tps=9.8
2026-03-17T09:20:01Z admission:reject id=abc124 reason=burst_credits_exhausted tps=12.3 limit=10
2026-03-17T09:20:05Z admission:reject id=abc125 reason=burst_credits_exhausted tps=14.1 limit=10
2026-03-17T09:20:12Z worker_latency WARNING p99=2.1s
```

taylor: Pool config: `fluxpay-prod-pool` model=gpt-rlf-3-large quant=4bit min_workers=2 max_workers=8 autoscale_policy=utilization headroom=0.1 burst_credits=1000

priya: Looks like client TPS temporarily spiked to ~14 which is above the tps cap 10. Burst credits at 0 explains rejects. Options: increase burst_credits for the pool, raise headroom so autoscaler keeps more idle capacity, or add a fallback routing rule to a cheaper/smaller variant during spikes.

samir: Agree. Two quick mitigation steps we can do now: 1) top-up burst_credits to give breathing room; 2) bump headroom to 0.25 so autoscaler keeps spare VMs while we investigate. I'll do step 1 if billing allows.

billing_bot: FYI — FluxPay contract: dedicated pool includes 5k burst credits/month. Usage today: 4,980. Additional credits require approval or a temporary quota increase from finance.

support_junior: Also seeing a client-side error they forwarded: `{"error":"rate_limited","message":"token-per-second limit exceeded"}` — they retried aggressively and created a short sustained overload. Suggest recommending exponential backoff and jitter on client.

priya: Implementation commands (internal):```bash
# top up burst credits (temporary)
rictl billing credit topup --customer fluxpay --pool fluxpay-prod-pool --amount 3000
# increase headroom (keeps more spare workers)
rictl pools update fluxpay-prod-pool --headroom 0.25
# add fallback routing to smaller model
rictl routing add --pool fluxpay-prod-pool --when "admission_reject" --fallback gpt-rlf-3-small
```

samir: I applied a temporary top-up of 3000 credits and bumped headroom to 0.25. Observability shows admission rejects dropping after ~2 minutes. Also enabled fallback routing to `gpt-rlf-3-small` for overload cases.

devopsbot: alert: fluxpay-prod-pool admission_reject_rate dropped from 82% -> 6% (09:22 -> 09:28). p99 latency improved from 2.1s -> 740ms.

taylor: Nice. Next: need to schedule a post-incident follow-up to decide long-term changes: increase baseline headroom for their profile, update autoscale policy to consider request rate (not just utilization), and add client-side guidance for 429 handling.

support_junior: I'll open a support ticket with step-by-step mitigations we applied and ask FluxPay to implement client retries + jitter. Also opened finance ticket to approve permanent bump to monthly burst credits.

samir: For the postmortem let's capture repro steps. Recommended repro: run small steady load at 9 TPS then blast 20 TPS for 90s to see credit drain and admission behavior. Example test script:```python
# simple repro (python)
import requests, time
url = 'https://api.redwood-inference/v1/generate'
headers = {'Authorization':'Bearer REPLACE'}
# warm up
for _ in range(50): requests.post(url, json={'model':'gpt-rlf-3-large','input':'hi'})
# spike
for _ in range(200): requests.post(url, json={'model':'gpt-rlf-3-large','input':'spam'})
```

priya: Add to the runbook: monitor `burst_credits` gauge, `admission_reject_rate`, `tps` and `worker_idle_fraction` when evaluating headroom changes. Recommend a headroom of 20-30% for low-latency customers with bursty traffic profiles.

taylor: Good. Closing the thread for now — mitigation applied and customer notified. Leaving follow-up actions: finance approval (ticket# FIN-4521), postmortem scheduled 2026-03-18 16:00 UTC, adjust runbook. :white_check_mark:
